verdict.rationale: cubic documents its own noise-reduction mechanisms. Thumbs up/down reactions help it 'calibrate what's useful vs noise', replies teach it what to do differently, ignore patterns in cubic.yaml narrow what gets reviewed, auto-resolve closes fixed findings, and a Datadog integration checks findings against production logs to cut false positives. But nothing in the evidence covers comment deduplication or severity labels, and there is no measured false-positive rate. Missing for 10: severity labels on findings, deduplication of repeated comments, independent or hands-on evidence of low false-positive rates.

support.subject: As an engineering lead, the reviewer keeps noise low — few false positives, deduplicated comments, severity labels — so my team doesn't tune it out

citations.quote: Thumbs up/down help cubic calibrate what's useful vs noise for your specific codebase
Type a response explaining what cubic should do differently, and it remembers for next time
Enable automatic thread resolution to close findings when the issue is fixed
Now you can connect Datadog, and cubic agents will check whether your production logs confirm their findings.
becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents
